PROCUREMENT DOCUMENTATION GUIDELINE

Stratified Developments – Developer's Management Period
Document No. [PFMSB/GL/YYYY/NNN] Version 1.0 (Draft for approval)
Issued by Operations, PR1MA Facilities Management Sdn Bhd (PFMSB) Effective date [DD/MM/YYYY]
Applies to Stratified developments (strata schemes under the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757)) managed by PFMSB during the developer's management period, for use by the appointed Property Manager Related forms PRF, RFQ, QA and PO templates (2026)

1. PURPOSE

This guideline sets one procurement process for every stratified development that PR1MA Facilities Management Sdn Bhd (PFMSB) manages during the developer's management period, to be applied by the Property Manager appointed for that development. It makes sure that every purchase of a service or material is requested, approved, competitively quoted, analysed and ordered in a fixed sequence, using the same four forms, so that spending from the property accounts can be traced and defended at audit and at handover to the JMB / MC. The guideline is aligned with the Strata Management Act 2013 (Act 757), the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and the KPKT Garis Panduan Kaedah Perolehan Pihak Pengurusan Bangunan Berstrata (2020) (the KPKT Guideline). Where this guideline is silent, the KPKT Guideline applies.

2. SCOPE AND APPLICATION

  • Applies only to stratified developments during the developer's management period, and to all works, supplies and services purchased for the development from its Maintenance Account or Sinking Fund Account, whether recurring (cleaning, security, lift maintenance, landscaping, pest control) or one-off (repairs, replacement, supply).

  • Is to be used by the Property Manager appointed for each development, who must be registered with the Board of Valuers, Appraisers, Estate Agents and Property Managers (LPPEH) and who carries out each step on behalf of PFMSB. PFMSB staff use it only to review, recommend or approve. It does not apply to non-stratified (landed) properties or to developments where a JMB or MC has taken over management.

  • Does not replace a written agreement already executed by both parties. Where one exists, its terms govern the transaction and this guideline governs only how the purchase was requested and approved.

  • The estimated total value of the requirement decides the procurement method, following KPKT Guideline para 10 and Table 2:

    1. Petty cash: supplies only, up to RM500 per bill, from a float of not more than RM3,000. The float is set by the CEO, and each claim is approved by the Assistant General Manager (Operations) before reimbursement. A valid receipt is required. The PRF, RFQ, QA and PO are not required.

      Direct purchase: works, supplies or services up to RM3,000. An approved PRF and a PO are still required. Steps 2 and 3 do not apply. Rotate vendors from the vendor register where practicable.

      Quotation: above RM3,000 and up to RM100,000. The full four-step process in Section 5 applies, with at least three written quotations from vendors registered with SSM and, where relevant, CIDB, Suruhanjaya Tenaga, DOSH (JKKP), KDN, BPKU or MOF.

      Tender: above RM100,000. An open tender is advertised in at least one main Malay or English newspaper and displayed on the development notice board, following KPKT Guideline para 14 and its tender document format. The approved PRF authorises the tender in place of the RFQ.

      Emergency: see Section 8.

  • Property-specific forms use the property code in the reference number (for example PRBK for Residensi PR1MA @ Bukit Katil). Each property replaces the code and letterhead but keeps the layout and wording.

3. DEFINITIONS

Term Meaning
PRF Procurement Requisition Form. The internal request for approval to procure. It records the need, urgency, budget and funding account.
RFQ Request for Quotation. The written invitation sent to selected vendors to quote against one standard scope, issued only after the PRF is approved.
QA Quotation Analysis. The side-by-side comparison of quotations against each other, the approved budget and the previous purchase, ending in a recommendation.
PO Purchase Order. The order issued to the appointed vendor after the QA is approved. It is governed by the Purchase Order Terms and Conditions.
Developer's management period As defined in Part IV of Act 757: the period from the date vacant possession of a parcel is delivered to a purchaser until one month after the JMB is established, or such later time as the Commissioner of Buildings (COB) allows. During this period the development is managed by PFMSB through the appointed Property Manager.
Maintenance Account / Sinking Fund Account The accounts the developer must open for each development under sections 10 and 11 of Act 757, from which expenses are paid. The PRF states which account is used; the PO shows the account payable.

5. PROCEDURE

STEP 1 PROCUREMENT REQUISITION FORM (PRF)

Purpose: obtain approval before any service or material is procured

  1. Raise the PRF as soon as a need is identified and before any vendor is approached for a price commitment. Enter the PRF number from the property register (PRBK/PRF: YYYY/MM/NNN).

  2. Complete Section 1 and 2: project, service or item, location, requester, and the justification. Tick Urgent or Normal, state whether an insurance claim is involved, and record the meeting instruction where the work arises from a meeting.

  3. Define the requirement in Section 4 in the standard format: description, scope of work, work area, job scope, service frequency, contract period, quantity and SST. This wording is carried unchanged into the RFQ, QA and PO.

  4. Complete Section 3 for this stage: list the vendors proposed to be invited (at least three) and an indicative amount taken from the approved budget or the previous purchase. Leave the recommendation column as "to be determined at Quotation Analysis". The note on supporting quotations does not apply until Step 3.

  5. Complete Section 5 (available budget): approved budget, amount utilised to date, balance, amount of this requisition and balance after. If the budget is insufficient, state the proposed source of funds or reallocation.

  6. Route for signature: Building Executive prepares, Assistant General Manager (Operations) recommends, CEO approves and states the funding account in Section 6.

Output: approved PRF. Only this authorises the RFQ.

STEP 2 REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ)

Purpose: obtain comparable written quotations from vendors approved in the PRF

  1. Prepare the RFQ on the RFQ template, copying the requirement from the approved PRF word for word. Quote the PRF number on the RFQ.

  2. Verification: the Registered Property Manager checks the scope, statutory and licensing requirements and the required vendor documents, then signs the issuer block.

  3. Issue the same RFQ, on the same day, in writing (email) to every vendor listed in the PRF, with one closing date and time. Adding or replacing a vendor needs the written approval of the Assistant General Manager (Operations), recorded on the PRF.

  4. Handle clarifications in writing. Share every question and reply with all invited vendors. Hold a site briefing only if the RFQ states it, and record attendance.

  5. Receive and log quotations in the RFQ register with the date and time of receipt. Do not open or discuss prices before the closing time. Late quotations are not considered.

Output: quotations from at least three vendors, logged, with the issued RFQ and vendor correspondence.

STEP 3 QUOTATION ANALYSIS (QA)

Purpose: compare like with like and recommend one vendor with reasons

  1. Standardise the Bill of Quantity so every vendor is priced on the same scope. Record corrections to arithmetic or SST treatment; do not change a vendor's unit prices.

  2. Complete the comparison table: unit price and total for each vendor, grand total, validity period, payment terms and contact person.

  3. Complete Section 3 of the QA: compare the recommended quotation with the approved budget and the previous purchase, stating the difference in RM and in percent.

  4. Write the recommendation: name the vendor, the amount and the reason (lowest price, relevant experience, current performance). If the vendor is not the lowest, or fewer than three quotations were received, the reason must be explicit.

  5. Complete the document checklist for quotations, catalogue, scope of works, warranty information, company registration (SSM, Form 9, 13, 24 or 49), relevant licences or registrations (CIDB, Suruhanjaya Tenaga, DOSH, KDN, as applicable), the signed Supplier Integrity Declaration and company profile.

  6. Amount above the PRF estimate: if the recommended amount exceeds the PRF estimate by more than the tolerance in Section 9, revise and re-approve the PRF before the QA goes forward.

  7. Route for signature: Building Executive prepares, Assistant General Manager (Operations) recommends, CEO approves.

Output: approved QA naming the appointed vendor and the approved amount.

STEP 4 PURCHASE ORDER (PO)

Purpose: commit to the appointed vendor on written terms

  1. Issue the PO only after the QA is approved. The Registered Property Manager prepares it; Assistant General Manager (Operations) recommends; CEO approves.

  2. Fill the PO from the approved documents: vendor details and SST number from the approved quotation, requirement text from the PRF, PRF reference number, delivery point and date, payment term, and the Maintenance Account or Sinking Fund Account (as stated in the PRF) as the account payable. The PO amount may not exceed the approved QA amount.

  3. Tick and enclose the PO attachments: Detail Scope of Works, and Service Level and Non-Compliance.

  4. Send the original PO to the vendor for acceptance. The vendor signs, has the PO witnessed, adds the company chop and returns it within seven (7) days.

  5. Release work or delivery only against the signed PO. Before payment, the Building Executive confirms completion or delivery, with photographs before and after for works. The vendor must send invoices to the purchaser's address, quoting the PO number; payment is made within the term stated on the PO.

Output: accepted PO and a complete procurement file.

6. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Role Responsibility in the procurement process
Building Executive Raises the PRF; prepares and issues the RFQ; receives, logs and safeguards quotations; standardises the Bill of Quantity; prepares the QA; confirms completion of the work or delivery.
Registered Property Manager Verifies the RFQ before issue; confirms scope, statutory and licensing requirements; prepares and issues the PO; keeps the procurement file complete.
Assistant General Manager, Operations Recommends the PRF, QA and PO; checks budget availability and consistency across the four documents; reviews the procurement registers each month.
Chief Executive Officer, PFMSB Approves the PRF, QA and PO; approves exceptions to this guideline.
Vendor Quotes against the RFQ as issued; does not start any work or delivery until a signed PO is received; accepts the PO and its Terms and Conditions.

7. CONTROLS

  • No commitment before approval. Staff and the property manager must not instruct work, place an order or promise an award before the relevant approval is in place.

  • No splitting. A requirement must not be divided into smaller purchases to avoid the process or an approval level.

  • Same scope for every vendor. Vendors are not given a different scope, price information or closing date from other vendors.

  • Conflict of interest. Anyone with a personal interest in a vendor declares it in writing to the Assistant General Manager (Operations) and takes no part in evaluating that vendor. Every Property Manager staff member involved in procurement signs an integrity declaration, based on KPKT Guideline Lampiran A, on appointment.

  • Vendor integrity declaration. Every RFQ or tender document encloses the Supplier Integrity Declaration (KPKT Guideline Lampiran B). A quotation returned without it, signed, is not considered.

  • Registered vendors only. Vendors must be registered with SSM and hold the licence or registration the work requires, for example DOSH for lifts, KDN for security, CIDB for works and Suruhanjaya Tenaga for electrical work (KPKT Guideline para 5.5).

  • Vendor register. The Property Manager keeps a vendor register for each development (KPKT Guideline Lampiran C), registers a vendor before inviting it, records its performance, and may remove a vendor whose performance is poor (para 9.5).

  • Notice to purchasers. The Property Manager displays a notice of each quotation or tender, and of its result (vendor and amount), on the development notice board (KPKT Guideline para 9.4).

  • Segregation of duties. The person who prepares a document does not approve it; the person who requests a purchase does not approve payment.

  • Budget first. No PRF is approved without the budget check in Section 5 of the PRF. Spending from the Sinking Fund follows the property's own approval rules in addition to this guideline.

  • Document consistency. The requirement text and SST rate must be the same in all four documents (see Section 10). Any difference is resolved before the next stage.

  • Changes after approval. A change in scope, quantity, vendor or amount needs a revised PRF (or a written variation under the PO Terms and Conditions) and fresh approval before it is acted on.

8. URGENT PROCUREMENT

Where there is a risk to life or the safety of occupants, serious damage to common property, disruption of a critical operation, loss of access to critical common areas, or a natural disaster, fire or disease outbreak (KPKT Guideline para 7.4), for example lift entrapment, loss of water supply, fire system failure or flooding, the Property Manager may instruct the minimum works needed to make the situation safe. The emergency limit is RM10,000 or 20% of the current annual budget, whichever is higher (KPKT Guideline Table 2). The sequence is then:

  1. Inform the Assistant General Manager (Operations) immediately and record the instruction, time and reason in writing (email or message log).

  2. Raise a PRF marked Urgent and obtain approval within [2] working days. Where the vendor has already attended, state this in Section 2.4.

  3. Obtain at least two written quotations where time allows. Otherwise the relevant building-services contractor or a suitable specialist contractor may be appointed without calling other quotations (KPKT Guideline para 15). Record the reason in the QA and obtain CEO approval of the single-source appointment.

  4. Issue the PO on approval of the QA. Urgent works cover only what is needed to make the situation safe; permanent repairs follow the normal process. Spending above the emergency limit needs CEO ratification. Within one (1) month of the works, the Property Manager submits a detailed report (cause, works done, vendor, cost, and photographs before and after) to the Assistant General Manager (Operations). The report is kept for handover to the JMB and tabled at the next general meeting where one is held.

11. RECORDS AND FILING

  • Keep one procurement file per PRF number, in the property management office, containing: PRF; RFQ and the vendor invitation emails; clarifications; all quotations received; QA with its attachments; PO and the vendor's accepted copy; delivery or completion evidence; invoice and payment record.

  • Keep running registers for PRF, RFQ, QA and PO numbers at each property. The number format is PREFIX/TYPE: YYYY/MM/NNN, where NNN is the running number maintained in the register.

  • Copy each approved PRF, QA and PO to the Assistant General Manager (Operations) for monitoring. The registers are reviewed each month.

  • Retain files for [7] years and hand over the complete files for the property to the JMB / MC at handover, as part of the handover documentation.
